knowledge_units.context_summary: The paper analyzes the Cauchy problem for two-dimensional nonlinear nonlocal wave equations modeling anti-plane shear motions. It establishes conditions for global existence or finite-time blow-up of solutions for initial data in L2 Sobolev spaces. The nonlocal nature is defined by a convolution kernel with a Fourier transform satisfying specific growth conditions.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The paper outlines its structure, covering the formulation of nonlocal elasticity, local and global existence theories, and finite-time blow-up. It defines the Fourier transform, inverse Fourier transform, and Sobolev space norms used in the analysis. The text explains that nonlocal elasticity was developed to address the lack of intrinsic length scales in conventional elasticity, which prevents accurate modeling of small-scale effects like wave dispersion and stress singularity.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The text derives the equation of motion for anti-plane shear motions in a nonlocally elastic medium by defining the relationship between local and nonlocal stress tensors. It establishes that for isotropic materials, the strain energy density depends solely on the squared gradient of the out-of-plane displacement. The resulting scalar partial differential equation incorporates a convolution integral to represent nonlocal effects, reducing to the conventional quasilinear wave equation when the kernel is a Dirac measure.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The initial value problem for the nonlocal wave equation is reformulated as a system of Banach space-valued ordinary differential equations to establish local well-posedness. Specific Sobolev and Lipschitz lemmas are applied to control nonlinear terms involving the gradient of the displacement. Theorem 3.7 proves local existence and uniqueness for initial data in Sobolev spaces with regularity s > 2.
